#2281. Gattuso ritrova il Napoli al Maradona: con la Lazio dopo i duelli al Milan

Il tecnico biancoceleste ha affrontato quattro volte gli azzurri dalla panchina rossonera; domenica giocherà alle 12:30.

Gattuso tornerà allo stadio Maradona da avversario del Napoli con la Lazio. Secondo quanto riportato da CalcioNapoli24, I biancocelesti saranno ospiti degli azzurri domenica 8 novembre alle 12:30. Per il tecnico sarà un confronto con la squadra che ha allenato in passato.

La trasferta riporterà l’allenatore biancoceleste in uno stadio che conosce bene, questa volta sulla panchina opposta a quella del Napoli. Alla partita si accompagna così il significato personale del ritorno contro la sua ex squadra.

Gattuso ha già affrontato il Napoli quattro volte da allenatore del Milan. Il bilancio complessivo riportato è di una vittoria, due pareggi e una sconfitta: numeri che descrivono un equilibrio nei confronti con gli azzurri.

L’unico successo indicato è arrivato in Coppa Italia. Il dato distingue la vittoria ottenuta nella competizione dalle gare disputate in campionato.

#2279. Cristiano Ronaldo lascia la Nazionale portoghese: tutte le reazioni

Dopo vent'anni, 234 presenze e 146 gol l'avventura di Cristiano Ronaldo con la maglia della Nazionale portoghese si è chiusa oggi. Ad annunciarlo lo stesso campione con un messaggio pubblicato sui propri canali social.

Di seguito vi proponiamo tutte le reazioni alla decisione dell'ex campione di Manchester United, Real Madrid e Juventus!

Ore 14:43, Jorge Mendes - Tramite X arrivano anche le parole di chi ha accompagnato Cristiano Ronaldo nel corso di tutta la sua carriera, l'agente Jorge Mendes: "Il più grande simbolo del Portogallo e del mondo, ha definito un'era. Lo dico ancora una volta: Cristiano Ronaldo è il miglior giocatore di sempre nella storia del calcio mondiale. Tutti noi portoghesi diciamo: grazie Cristiano. Non ce ne sarà mai un altro come te".

Ore 13:39, Gonçalo Ramos - "Grazie di tutto" è il breve messaggio che Gonçalo Ramos, attuale centravanti del Milan ha voluto lasciare in calce al post con il quale CR7 ha dato l'addio alla Nazionale.

Ore 13:34, Nani - In campo insieme in 130 occasioni, sia con la maglia del Manchester United che con quella del Portogallo, CR7 e Nani sono state una delle coppie di attaccanti più prolifiche delle ultime decadi. Ecco il messaggio che Nani ha voluto rivolvere all'ex compagno: "Congratulazioni, fratello, per questo splendido percorso! Ci hai ispirato tutti e ci hai fatto credere che, come portoghesi, potevamo essere i migliori al mondo. Ci hai resi orgogliosi di noi stessi, come popolo e come squadra. Sei e sarai sempre un punto di riferimento per tutti noi che ti seguiamo e che condividiamo momenti meravigliosi con te, dentro e fuori dal campo. La Nazionale è l'apice delle nostre carriere e sono incredibilmente orgoglioso di aver fatto parte della sua storia. Per me, sei il migliore di tutti i tempi, non solo per il giocatore che sei stato e per tutto ciò che hai dato alla nostra Nazionale, ma anche per ciò che hai rappresentato per tutti noi. Anche quando spesso non eravamo d'accordo, siamo sempre cresciuti, migliorati e abbiamo imparato. E ti dobbiamo anche questo. Per tutto questo, posso solo dire: grazie mille, Capitano! Ciò che hai fatto per il Portogallo e per tutti noi non sarà mai dimenticato".

Ore 13:30, Reinaldo Teixeira - Queste le parole del presidente della Liga Portugal, la massima serie del calcio portoghese, all'addio di Cristiano Ronaldo alla Nazionale: "La parabola di Cristiano Ronaldo, come persona e come calciatore, è da tempo indissolubilmente legata al nome del Portogallo. È - e continuerà ad essere per molti anni - un simbolo della nostra identità culturale e dell'inestimabile valore che apporta a questa passione condivisa da milioni di cittadini in tutto il mondo: il calcio. Il suo addio alla nazionale è una decisione, come tante altre nella sua vita, che ha un profondo impatto su molte persone a livello globale. Non ho dubbi nell'affermare che sia una personalità che trascende paesi e culture, qualcosa di cui noi portoghesi possiamo essere orgogliosi, sempre per il modo in cui si è affermato: come uno di noi. Ciò che ci hai dato non può essere racchiuso in poche righe o commenti. E continuerai a darci. Sono convinto che, pur avendo definitivamente appeso al chiodo la maglia della nazionale, il sentimento e la consapevolezza di essere portoghese rimarranno impressi sulla tua pelle e nelle tue emozioni. Cristiano Ronaldo saprà intrecciare il suo declino da giocatore con l'industria e l'arte che ha lasciato un segno indelebile da quando il suo nome ha iniziato a suscitare meraviglia. La sua storia sarà eterna, così come la nostra gratitudine per ciò che ci ha donato e continuerà a donarci. A nome della Liga Portugal e a nome mio personale, grazie di cuore!"

Ore 13:28, Bruno Fernandes - Arriva, via Instagram anche il post di Bruno Fernandes, compagno di Nazionale di CR7 e attuale capitano del Manchester United: "Grazie per avermi ispirato. È stato un privilegio poter condividere i grandi momenti della nostra Nazionale con il mio idolo d'infanzia".

Ore 13:26, Neymar - Una sola parola è quella che Neymar ha scelto di usare per commentare la notizia dell'addio di CR7 alla Nazionale portoghese in calce al post del fenomeno lusitano: "Leggenda".

Ore 12:50, Pedro Proença - Anche Pedro Proença, presidente della Federcalcio portoghese, ha pubblicato un lungo messaggio indirizzato a Cristiano Ronaldo dopo la notizia del suo addio alla Nazionale Portoghese: "Per il Portogallo, Cristiano Ronaldo sarà più di un semplice giocatore. Un uomo, un atleta, un modello, un eroe, un leader. Il nostro Capitano. Nel giorno in cui annuncia il suo ritiro dalla Nazionale, a nome della Federazione Calcistica Portoghese e di tutto il calcio portoghese, ringraziamo Cristiano Ronaldo per tutto ciò che ci ha dato. E ha dato tantissimo. Più delle vittorie, dei trofei e dei record, più dello status di giocatore più internazionale di tutti i tempi e di miglior marcatore della nostra storia, ciò che rimane è il suo esempio e la sua ispirazione. L'ispirazione di chi ha portato il Portogallo in tutto il mondo. Che, in ogni angolo del pianeta, ogni volta che si parlava del Portogallo, qualcuno nominasse Cristiano Ronaldo. E l'esempio per tutti coloro che sognano di migliorarsi ogni giorno. Come presidente della Federazione Calcistica Portoghese, ringrazio Cristiano Ronaldo per tutto il supporto dimostrato nell'ultimo anno e mezzo. Per le conversazioni e la vicinanza. Le porte della Federazione Calcistica Portoghese saranno sempre aperte per Cristiano Ronaldo. Grazie di tutto e di molto altro ancora. Per Sempre il nostro Capitano".

Ore 12:42, Antonio José Seguro - Arriva anche il messaggio del Presidente della Repubblica portoghese Antonio José Seguro alla notizia dell'addio alla Nazionale di Cristiano Ronaldo: "A nome del Portogallo, ringrazio Cristiano Ronaldo per come ha rappresentato la Nazionale, per aver ispirato il popolo portoghese e per aver portato il nome del Portogallo in tutto il mondo. Immagino che questo sia uno dei giorni più difficili della carriera sportiva di Cristiano Ronaldo, ma sono certo che, come è accaduto tante altre volte, abbia il popolo portoghese al suo fianco. So anche che il Portogallo continuerà a contare sul suo amore per il Paese, che rappresenterà sempre con la dedizione che ha profuso in ogni allenamento, in ogni partita, in ogni gol che ha riempito tutti di gioia. Tantissimi auguri, Cristiano. E grazie di cuore".

Ore 12:31, Katia Aveiro - C'è un velo di polemica nelle brevi parole scritte da Katia Aveiro, altra sorella di CR7 alla notizia della decisione di salutare la Nazionale portoghese da parte dell'ex campione di Real Madrid, Manchester United e Juventus: "Potrei dire tante cose. Ma solo il tempo le dirà. Ve lo dico io. È enorme, è gigantesco. È leggendario. Fino alla fine".

Ore 12:23, Luis Montenegro - Le reazioni alla notizia sull'addio di CR7 al Portogallo superano anche i confini del mondo del pallone. Queste le parole, diffusa via social, di Luis Montenegro, primo ministro del Portogallo: "Grazie! Quello che hai fatto in campo per il Portogallo risuonerà nell'eternità. E ora, fuori dal campo, continuerai comunque a essere il Portogallo nel mondo"

Ore 12:21, Elma Aveiro - "Il più grande orgoglio della mia vita. Ti amo. Sempre con te" è questo il primo post social legato all'addio di Cristiano Ronaldo alla maglia della Nazionale portoghese pubblicato via Instagram da Elma Aveiro, sorella del campione ex di Manchester United, Real Madrid e Juventus.

Ore 12:16, Pepe - Uno dei giocatori che più ha legato la propria carriera a quella di CR7 è stato senza dubbio Pepe. I due fra Nazionale e Real Madrid sono scesi in campo assieme in 348 partite, per un totale di 28.097 minuti fianco a fianco. Per questo quello dell'ex difensore è stato uno dei primi messaggio in risposta all'annuncio dell'addio di Ronaldo alla Nazionale portoghese: "È stato più che calcio. Grazie per tutto Cris".

Ore 12:11, Rio Ferdinand - Una delle prime reazioni alla notizia arriva da Rio Ferdinad, ex compagno di CR7 ai tempi dello United. Poche parole, quelle scritte in calce al post del campione lusitano, ma che danno il senso della carriera vissuta dal classe 1985: "È stato un film fratello".

#2278. Gds - Milan, i 50 mln di Adidas non sono di base. Inter batte cassa con Nike: cifre e scenari

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

L'Inter è pronta a battere cassa con Nike, fa sapere La Gazzetta dello Sport. È uno degli effetti del nuovo contratto tra Milan e Adidas da 50 milioni, che partirà dal 2028 e durerà 10 stagioni. Un accordo importantissimo, visto che l'accordo che i rossoneri avevano con Puma era da 24,5 milioni (da bilancio).

La rosea sottolinea che "è logico immaginare che quei 50 milioni incorporino bonus sportivi (per esempio la partecipazione alla Champions), il controvalore della fornitura di materiale (value in kind) e una quota da investire sull’attività promozionale (marketing fund). I contratti con gli sponsor tecnici sono molto complessi perché non si limitano, ovviamente, a riconoscere un valore per la presenza del logo sulle divise da gioco: se l’intesa, come nel caso del Milan, si estende alla vendita dei relativi prodotti, allora entrano in gioco i minimi garantiti e le royalties che scattano oltre una certa soglia di fatturato.

#2276. Generali Stadium: Inter e Milan insieme conviene? La risposta. Ricavi? Altro che 60 mln: cifre choc!

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Il nuovo Generali Stadium di Inter e Milan potrebbe cambiare radicalmente la capacità dei due club di generare ricavi e competere economicamente con le big europee.

È quanto emerge dall’analisi aggiornata di Football Benchmark, firmata dal CEO Andrea Sartori, che prova a rispondere a tre domande fondamentali: quanto può rendere il nuovo stadio, quanto costerà e perché continuare a condividerlo può essere la scelta più conveniente per Inter e Milan.

Il progetto ha compiuto un passo decisivo nel novembre 2025, quando i due club hanno completato l’acquisto di San Siro e delle aree circostanti dal Comune di Milano.

Il 29 ottobre 2026 è stato poi presentato il progetto del nuovo Generali Stadium, impianto da circa 71.500 posti destinato a sostituire l’attuale Meazza. L’inizio dei lavori è previsto nel 2028, mentre la prima partita dovrebbe essere disputata nella stagione 2031/32.

#2275. Birmingham City dodged bullet by not signing Middlesbrough man in the summer: Opinion

Birmingham City were said to be keen on landing the midfielder from Hadjuk Split in the last transfer window. However, the BCFC-linked man ended up joining fellow Championship side Middlesbrough instead.

Pukstas, 22, has since struggled for minutes at the Riverside Stadium and has played just 22 minutes for Kim Hellberg’s side since his switch to England. He is also currently out with a hamstring injury until early December which isn’t ideal.

Therefore, the Blues dodged a bullet by not signing the USA youth international and will be relieved that they didn’t fork out a hefty fee for his services. Boro paid £4.3million (via Transfermarkt) and handed him a long-term contract running until June 2031 but he has found it hard to get into their starting XI due to competition from the likes of Aidan Morris, Riley McGree and Sebastian Berhalter.

Birmingham City are sat in 3rd place in the table after 14 fixtures and slipped back into the play-offs after Wolves won 2-1 at Bristol City on Wednesday. They beat Millwall 3-0 at home last time out and take on Swansea City this weekend.

Birmingham City will have identified Pukstas as someone to bolster their midfield department. If he had joined BCFC, he would have given them more depth in the middle of the park.

At the age of 22, he has potential to grow and develop down the line. However, it wasn’t to be and the Blues were beaten to the punch by Middlesbrough.

Nevertheless, Chris Davies won’t be too disappointed now and he is well stocked up with options in Pukstas’ position. He has Paik Seung-ho, Tomoki Iwata, Jhon Solis and Taylor Gardner-Hickman at his disposal.

Max Bird joined instead of Pukstas in the end and he is slowly starting to prove his worth. The ex-Derby County and Bristol City man scored against Millwall earlier this week and is growing in confidence.

Birmingham City have enough options in midfield and also have Marc Leonard out injured. BCFC will get the chance to bolster their squad further in January.

The Blues are unlikely to look for another central midfielder this winter and will be happy with what they have. Instead, they are likely to look at attacking midfielders and wingers.

Davies’ men are on a roll right now and will be in good spirits. They are rock solid in defence and have the best defensive record in the division right now.

#2272. Nadal come LeBron e... Al Khelaifi. Chi sono le stelle degli altri sport entrate nel calcio

Alcuni campioni, anche dopo aver smesso di competere in campo, continuano a cercare fuori sfide altrettanto stimolanti. Rafael Nadal, a 40 anni suonati, sembra averne trovata una davvero prestigiosa, questa volta lontano dalla terra rossa. Il fuoriclasse maiorchino è pronto infatti a entrare nella dirigenza del Real Madrid, la squadra per cui non ha mai nascosto la propria simpatia e di cui era già socio onorario. Ieri, 4 novembre, il club di Florentino Perez ha ufficialmente proposto il suo ingresso nella Junta Directiva, il consiglio direttivo che guida le strategie della società merengue: la nomina dovrà essere ratificata dai soci il prossimo 21 novembre. Per uno dei più grandi sportivi di sempre, 22 titoli Slam, 92 tornei vinti e cinque Coppe Davis con la Spagna, si aprirebbe così un capitolo totalmente nuovo.

Quella di Nadal non sarebbe, però, una prima assoluta. Il calcio ha da tempo imparato ad attirare campioni provenienti da altri universi sportivi. Steve Nash, leggenda del basket NBA, è entrato per esempio nel gruppo proprietario dei Vancouver Whitecaps nel 2008. LeBron James ha invece scelto il Liverpool, acquistando nel 2011 una quota di minoranza poi confluita nella sua partecipazione al gruppo Fenway Sports. E ancora... Nel 2023 è arrivato Tom Brady: sette Super Bowl conquistati e un nuovo ruolo da azionista di minoranza del Birmingham City, oltre alla presidenza dell'Advisory Board. Nello stesso anno anche JJ Watt, ex stella del football americano, ha deciso di investire nel Burnley insieme alla moglie Kealia.

C'è poi una storia che incrocia proprio i due mondi di Nadal: quella di Nasser Al-Khelaifi, ex tennista professionista, divenuto assai più celebre come presidente del Paris Saint-Germain. La sua parabola, iniziata sui campi da tennis e proseguita attraverso gli investimenti di Qatar Sports Investments, racconta quanto possano essere imprevedibili le strade che portano dal campo fino alla scrivania. Va detto però che Nadal seguirà un percorso differente: non entrerà nel Real Madrid con una quota azionaria, ma per portare il suo prestigio, il suo blasone e la sua esperienza direttamente nella stanza dei bottoni.

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Dal Corriere dello Sport di oggi arriva anche un aggiornamento su quelli che dovrebbero essere i convocati di Roberto Mancini per i prossimi due impegni dell'Italia. Un gruppo diverso rispetto all'ultimo e di sicuro meno ampio, semplicemente perché i match da affrontare saranno due e non quattro. Si legge sul quotidiano:

"Il ct Mancini anticipa e già oggi dovrebbe diramare i convocati per la Nations. La lista è pronta o quasi. Gruppo ridotto a 26-27 azzurri, sei o sette in meno rispetto a settembre, perché sono solo due le partite, giovedì 12 al Meazza di Milano con la Francia di Zidane (si va verso il sold out) e domenica 15 a Bruxelles con il Belgio. L’Italia tenta l’ingresso ai quarti. Mancio ha qualche dubbio in attacco, ieri pomeriggio riunione zoom con lo staff. Si è fermato (già da una settimana) Retegui, saltando la Champions asiatica e l’ultimo turno di Saudi League: si aggiunge a Kean, Raspadori e Raimondo, indisponibili.

Riflessioni aperte su Scamacca, oggi di nuovo a disposizione per l’Atalanta in Conference. Il titolare è Pio Esposito. Sebastiano, suo fratello, gioca centravanti nel Sassuolo. Daniel Maldini si muove ormai da punta centrale. Difficili Lucca o Pinamonti. Sembra presto per l’oriundo Modica (Gimnasia), seguito dagli osservatori azzurri. Da registrare i ritorni di Zaniolo e Dimarco, un mese fa costretti a disertare per infortunio. Cristante in discussione. Il ct vuole vedere i giovani. Sicuro l’ingresso del milanista Cisse. Koleosho in dubbio, non sta bene. Zoma (Norimberga) si è operato alla spalla. Torna Pisilli. Palestra entra nella scia di Kayode. Di Lorenzo è fuori, sotto osservazione Floriani Mussolini, più avanti di Lulli. Dal gruppo U21 potrebbe salire forse Liberali".

#2269. Beukema in mixed zone: “Non possiamo prendere questi gol. Siamo arrabbiati”

Ecco le parole di Sam Beukema in mixed zone:

“Certo, vogliamo dimostrare questa risposta a tutti, ma anche a noi stessi, perché sappiamo le nostre qualità, abbiamo qualità dentro questo gruppo. Però, se non vinci e hai di nuovo un’altra delusione oggi, non è ovviamente facile. Non c’è tanto tempo, perché domenica c’è un’altra grande partita e ovviamente vogliamo chiudere questo periodo meno positivo. Questo è il nostro obiettivo e adesso dobbiamo recuperare, pensare alla prossima, riguardare bene i gol che abbiamo subito, imparare velocemente da questo e reagire domenica.

Perché, come ho detto prima, i dettagli fanno la differenza a questo livello. Due calci d’angolo così non sono possibili, dobbiamo riguardare subito questo perché non può succedere.

#2268. Wolves face spell without 22-year-old after midweek warning leads to injury

Wolves saw Jordan James forced off after 36 minutes in the 3-0 win over Cardiff City last Saturday, and he missed Wednesday’s victory at Bristol City as a result. The Express and Star has now confirmed the Welshman faces a short spell out with a hamstring injury.

James had complained of discomfort in his hamstring in the week leading up to the game, but he was cleared in scans and started. Further tests in the wake of his withdrawal ruled him out against the Robins, and the midfielder is set to sit out against Wrexham this Saturday too.

The 22-year-old, who had interest from Wrexham in the summer of 2025, will hope to return as soon as safely possible. James was not given a Wales call-up for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures, so he will have the break to rest up and recover.

James has not played the starring role many backed him for at Wolves after his fine stint with Leicester City last season. He had to wait until October 13th for his first league start, but his back-to-back starting XI selections in the Watford and Cardiff City clashes suggested he was beginning to find his place.

In the midweek win over Bristol City, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde was brought into the side in attacking midfield. Marshall Munetsi, who James has also been battling with for a start, was in a deeper midfield role alongside Andre.

Bellegarde does have competition for his place though. Mateus Mane will hope to reclaim a starting berth having been benched for four of the last five matches, while Rodrigo Gomes could be reintroduced as well.

Tawanda Chirewa offers energy off the bench, so Cesar Peixoto is not short of options despite James’ injury.

As touched on before, James hasn’t made the impact quite hoped for at Molineux yet. He has had to battle for his starting spot and two goals in 13 games means he isn’t replicating the productive form he showed at Leicester City (34 games, 11 goals, four assists).

However, from his spell with the Foxes and in his Birmingham City breakthrough beforehand, there is no doubt that the Wales international can be a real standout at this level. He will hope to rediscover his previous best with the Old Gold yet.

Providing no further setbacks emerge, James can use the international break to recover and work closely with Peixoto and his coaches to help him have a bigger impact.

Wanderers face Charlton Athletic in the first game after the break on November 21st. It remains to be seen if the loan midfielder is fit and ready for the return to action.

Zaccagni è fuori e Nuno Tavares è in dubbio per un affaticamento al flessore: la Lazio affronta un’emergenza sulla sinistra in vista della gara al Maradona. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Tavares non si è allenato nell’ultima seduta e Gattuso spera di recuperarlo all’ultimo momento.

Dal resto del gruppo arrivano segnali migliori. Cataldi non ha riportato conseguenze dopo il suo primo ingresso. Marusic e Rovella, dopo oltre due mesi, sono pronti a tornare in panchina al Maradona, secondo Il Messaggero.

Marusic risponderà anche alla convocazione della sua Nazionale durante la sosta. Per Gattuso, i due rientri rappresentano una notizia positiva mentre restano da gestire le assenze sulla sinistra.

#2264. Lazio, il calendario ora è in salita: dal Lecce al Como tra derby e Inter

Dopo la sosta i biancocelesti ospiteranno il Lecce e andranno a Torino; dal 6 dicembre inizierà la serie di sfide più impegnative.

La Lazio di Gattuso si prepara a un calendario in salita: dopo la partita di domenica e due impegni alla ripresa dalla sosta, tra il 6 dicembre e il 10 gennaio arriveranno sfide con Atalanta, Roma, Frosinone, Inter, Fiorentina e Como. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Finora il tecnico ha affrontato sette delle ultime dieci squadre di Serie A. La prossima serie di gare offrirà un quadro diverso.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Alla ripresa del campionato, i biancocelesti riceveranno il Lecce all’Olimpico. Seguirà il viaggio a Torino per affrontare i granata: due partite che precederanno il tratto più impegnativo del programma, ricostruito dal Messaggero.

La sequenza comincerà il 6 dicembre con l’Atalanta in casa. Sarri è indicato alla guida dei bergamaschi, pur con un’incertezza sulla sua permanenza in panchina fino a quella partita. Poi arriverà il derby, con i tifosi attesi di nuovo a riempire la Curva Nord.

Il 18 dicembre la Lazio giocherà sul campo del Frosinone di Alvini, allo Stirpe. In seguito è prevista la finale a San Siro contro l’Inter, nel periodo che comprende anche la Supercoppa.

#2263. Sembrava pronto per la rinascita della Triestina, ma Allegretti sposta il progetto Club Milano

Nei mesi scorsi il suo nome era stato accostato alla Triestina, per la rinascita del club, ma alla fine gli alabardati hanno puntato su Gaetano Fontana. Riccardo Allegretti, però, non si è fermato, ed è stato da poco nominato nuovo trainer del Club Milano, formazione militante nel campionato di Serie D, Girone B. Di seguito, la nota:

"La società Club Milano SSD aRL comunica di aver affidato la guida tecnica della Prima Squadra a Riccardo Allegretti.

Nato a Milano nel 1978 ed ex centrocampista di Triestina, Como, Lecco ed Empoli tra le altre, Riccardo Allegretti ha collezionato 68 presenze in Serie A e 253 in Serie B, mettendo a segno 44 reti totali in carriera.

Una volta conclusa l’esperienza da giocatore, Riccardo Allegretti ha intrapreso la carriera da allenatore conseguendo la Licenza UEFA A. Dopo alcune parentesi tra FC Cologno e Primorje FC, tra il 2019 e il 2020 ha seduto sulla panchina del Monza U17 prima e Monza U19 poi.

Nel 2021 è approdato alla neonata FC Clivense, iscritta al campionato di Terza Categoria dopo l’esclusione del Chievo dai campionati professionistici. Con la società veronese ha scalato le varie categorie, arrivando a vincere un campionato di Eccellenza nel 2023. Tra il 2024 e il 2025 ha poi guidato il rinato Chievo Verona in Serie D.

Oggi, alle ore 14:30, Riccardo Allegretti dirigerà il suo primo allenamento al Pero Sporting Club. La società ringrazia il mister per aver accettato con entusiasmo l’incarico e gli dà ufficialmente il benvenuto".

#2261. Derby County must turn to 43-year-old if they sack John Eustace: Opinion

Derby County have won only one of their first 14 league fixtures and they are in the drop zone along with Preston North End and Burnley. DCFC are seven points from safety behind Watford and Charlton Athletic following their 4-0 loss at home to Norwich City last time out.

The Rams’ hierarchy have a big decision to make about the future of head coach Eustace. If they are to sack the ex-Birmingham City and Blackburn Rovers man, there is only one man for the job at Pride Park.

Step forward Rob Edwards, who has been available since his shock summer sacking by Wolves and he has been weighing up his options in the game since. He has been carefully waiting for the right opportunity to arise and hasn’t rushed back into work yet.

The Telford-born man is a vastly experienced coach in the EFL and may feel he has a point to prove after his surprise dismissal from Molineux in June. At the age of 43, he is still young for a manager and he has overseen over 250 games from the dugout so far in his career.

If Derby County cut ties with Eustace, there aren’t that many available options at the moment. It seems unlikely DCFC would get someone like Steven Gerrard, Sean Dyche or Steve Cooper.

Paul Heckingbottom, Gary Rowett, Matt Bloomfield or Liam Manning would all be underwhelming and it costs money to get someone already employed. Therefore, Edwards seems the most obvious candidate.

He knows the league well, understands what it takes to get out of it and is someone who could help transform the Rams’ fortunes. As well as Wolves, he has also managed the likes of Forest Green Rovers, Watford, Luton Town and Middlesbrough.

Edwards’ best spell came at Kenilworth Road and he guided the Hatters to promotion to the Premier League against the odds during his time in Bedfordshire. They beat Coventry City on penalties in the play-off final.

Derby County need to act fast if they are to land Edwards. The longer DCFC leave it, the further adrift they could be cut and the less attractive they would become for prospective Eustace replacements.

Edwards has been linked with a switch to Wrexham recently and was also in the frame for the recent Burnley post. If the Rams lose again on Friday night to Bolton Wanderers, it would be hard to see Eustace surviving.

#2259. Signori e la Nazionale: «Quella ferita non si chiuderà mai», ritorno in azzurro

Il nuovo incarico nell’Under 20 allevia il dolore degli anni difficili; dopo la chiamata, il primo pensiero è andato a Tina.

Beppe Signori torna in azzurro: Malagò gli ha affidato il ruolo di capo delegazione della Nazionale Under 20. L’ex attaccante, che attendeva da tempo una chiamata nel calcio, si prepara al debutto del 12 novembre a Padova contro il Portogallo. Il nuovo incarico riporta con sé l’entusiasmo per una maglia indossata da protagonista e il ricordo degli anni segnati da una vicenda giudiziaria che ha condizionato profondamente la sua vita.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

In vista della partita contro il Portogallo, Signori descrive sensazioni diverse da quelle vissute da calciatore: «È un debutto diverso, ma per certi versi molto più emozionante. Sono carico di entusiasmo, sento una grande responsabilità».

Alla proposta di Malagò, racconta, non ha mai pensato di rispondere negativamente. La considerava un’opportunità attesa a lungo e non avrebbe voluto rinunciarvi per orgoglio o per la rabbia legata a ciò che aveva subito: «Assolutamente mai! Era una grande opportunità, l'aspettavo da tanto».

Signori, intervistato da Il Resto del Carlino, vuole partire da determinazione, sacrificio e passione. Intende aiutare i giovani a comprendere la responsabilità di rappresentare la propria nazione e l’orgoglio di vestire l’azzurro. A suo giudizio, oggi i ragazzi sono abituati ad avere tutto, mentre la sua generazione doveva conquistarsi ogni cosa.

Alla domanda se l’azzurro abbia perso fascino dopo tre Mondiali mancati, risponde senza esitazioni: «No, l'azzurro non passa mai. Quella maglia ti dà una sensazione forte, unica». Ricorda la competizione per un posto ai suoi tempi, quando tra gli attaccanti c’erano anche Baggio, Zola, Mancini, Vialli e Casiraghi. Per questo ritiene che i giovani debbano riconoscere il privilegio di giocare per l’Italia e dimostrare di esserne all’altezza, nonostante le distrazioni esterne e una società orientata, secondo lui, al tutto e subito.

#2258. Renica difende Allegri: "Non è solo colpa sua. Ha ereditato un Napoli da rinnovare"

Alessandro Renica, ex difensore del Napoli, ha preso la parola nel corso di 'Terzo Tempo Champions', trasmissione in onda su Televomero, per analizzare la situazione critica degli azzurri. Di seguito le sue dichiarazioni all'indomani della sconfitta col Porto.

"La partita del Napoli è un grande rammarico. Il Porto era alla portata. Ci sono stati momenti in cui ha fraseggiato bene, però non si possono prendere dei gol così, con gli avversari che saltano liberamente in area. Gli azzurri non possono continuare con questi cali di tensione. Il discorso sarebbe più ampio, perché la colpa non è solo di Allegri, ha ereditato una squadra con una certa età, spesso con giocatori infortunati".

Sulla sconfitta in Portogallo, Renica ha poi aggiunto: "Quando prendi quei gol il morale va a terra. Allegri si trova una squadra che già l'anno scorso è stata martoriata dagli infortuni. Andava un po' rinnovata in alcuni ruoli. Hojlund non ha un sostituito adeguato, s'insiste con Lucca perché non c'è un'alternativa di qualità. La società non ha rinforzato la squadra in modo ragionato. Il Napoli deve ritrovare compattezza, altrimenti si passeranno momenti poco belli. Anche contro la Juventus c’è stato un buon primo tempo, poi un errore serio ha compromesso la partita".

#2257. Sheffield United man to attract transfer ‘interest’ in January window, says reporter

Sheffield United could face a battle to keep hold of the England youth international in the upcoming January transfer window amid potential attention from other clubs. He is under contract at SUFC until June 2028 meaning he still has just under two years left to run down on his deal at Bramall Lane.

Peck, 22, has become a key player for the Blades in the Championship under the guidance of head coach Chris Wilder. He has made 16 appearances for the South Yorkshire outfit in all competitions this season, 14 of which have come in the league, and he has chipped in with four goals and three assists.

Oxley has shared this update on his situation, as per a report by BBC Sport: “Peck’s stock is high, and rising. He has become a regular in the England under-21 side, he’s one of the first names on the Blades team sheet, and his underlying shooting, passing, possession and defending statistics show he ranks as one of the Championship’s best players in his position.

“He was coveted by Premier League clubs last summer, and you’d imagine he will be the subject of interest once again in January, especially after United sold a trio of stars pre-season to help balance the books.”

Sheffield United won’t want to lose Peck anytime soon, especially halfway through this campaign. He is a valuable member of SUFC’s squad and has the capacity to grow and develop even further down the line.

West Ham were said to be keen on him in the summer after their relegation from the Premier League. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put beyond the last deadline in September.

Peck, who is from Worthing, has enjoyed plenty of game time with the Blades over recent times. He battles it out with the likes of Kalvin Phillips, Oli Arblaster and Joe Rothwell, among others, for minutes in Wilder’s starting XI.

He joined Sheffield United as a youngster back in 2021 after rising up through the academy at Arsenal. He has since played over 100 matches and was also loaned out to Oldham Athletic back in 2022 to get some more experience under his belt down in League Two.

Sheffield United’s chances of retaining the services of Peck in the long run will likely depend on whether they can reach the top flight. If they go up this term, he would probably stick around at SUFC.

If they stay in the second tier though, it would be a surprise if he stayed beyond next year. The Blades need to take advantage of his ability whilst they can.

Wilder’s men have been in good form recently and are genuine contenders for the play-offs if they can stay consistent. They beat Preston North End 3-2 last time out on Tuesday night with Peck scoring a hat-trick at Deepdale against the Lilywhites.

Sheffield United are now unbeaten in their last four and they are starting to build a bit of momentum now as they aim to get into the top eight. They are sat in 9th position in the table and they are only a point behind West Ham in 8th ahead of their upcoming match against Charlton Athletic away.

#2255. Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs

It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

Mount has spent the majority of his career playing further forward, either off the right or as a No. 10 but Carrick likes him in a fluid No. 8 role, a position Erik ten Hag had identified for the player only for persistent injuries to detonate those plans.

The logic is simple: Mount is mobile, can cover the ground, is adept under pressure, has line breaking passing, vision and a nose for goal. He is also a good presence in the dressing room and a leader in his own way. Watch him imparting advice to Shea Lacey as they walked back to the centre circle after the youngster’s goal opened the scoring against Rosenborg and you get a glimpse of that.

The question, of course, is whether he can stay fit long enough to impose those qualities that help to explain why Liverpool and Arsenal had also been so keen to sign him back in 2023 and Carrick’s predecessor Ruben Amorim was also such a fan.

With United’s summer budget only stretching so far, Carrick was always going to have to think on his feet in certain areas of the pitch.

What will be interesting to see over the coming weeks is whether the manager feels Mount is robust enough to complement Santos, fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo.

MASON MOUNT SCORES FOR MAN UNITED!He takes the ball with a quality turn, and curls it into the corner of the goal 🤩📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/M9ErA2HKbo

Much of the chatter among United fans at present centres on who the third midfield signing will be after Santos and Tielemans.

Given Mount’s injury record, it would be a significant risk not to recruit again in that department in the hope he could stay fit over a full season. Four options in two positions behind the No 10 of Fernandes sounds fine in principle but what happens if Mount’s season was to follow a similar trajectory to the previous three?

If United are going to strengthen in other areas, there will need to be compromises or alternative solutions that help to free up cash along the way but gambling in midfield may not be the best way to go.

With Champions League football to factor in this season, it is still hard to believe United will not seek to strengthen again in midfield but the club seem ready to take their time on that front. And all the while an assortment of names continue to fly around.

After spending £85m on Santos and Tielemans, a massive outlay on a third midfielder at this stage would be a bit of a surprise.

Could that negate a move for Real Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni? Alex Scott is greatly admired by United but Bournemouth are determined to keep him and have put a prohibitive pricetag on him.

AS Roma’s Manu Kone is not thought to have universal backing internally. Tyler Adams’ name has been floated again but the Bournemouth and US midfielder’s injury record counts against him.

There has not yet been evidence of a serious appetite to go for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, whom they considered signing last summer. Sander Berge at Fulham and Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha are among a number of other midfielders who have been linked with United.

Another midfield signing could well emerge but United are keeping their cards close to their chest. Whatever materialises, though, it will still not change the fact this is a huge season for Mount.

⚽️ Shea Lacey⚽️ Jacob Devaney⚽️ Harry Amass⚽️ Ethan Williams Four #MUAcademy prospects were on the scoresheet in Trondheim 🧬💙 pic.twitter.com/fguQ36ANTM

“It was a good day. Clean sheet, scoring goals and everyone coming through injury-free hopefully is everything you want. Keeping the players fit and improving through pre-season is amongst the most important things. You want to build through the pre-season and you have to manage to players differently. It is never going to be perfect but we scored some great goals and we are moving forward nicely.

“I thought we defended well as a team for the most part. A clean sheet is a beautiful thing. I think we are in a good place with four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup. As it stands right now, we are in a pretty good place.”

This is what the official start of the season will look like for Michael Carrick’s side:

August 22- Hull vs Manchester UnitedAugust 30- Manchester United vs IpswichSeptember 6- Everton vs Manchester UnitedSeptember 13- Manchester United vs Manchester CitySeptember 20- Fulham vs Manchester United

They face two of the three promoted sides on the first two weekends and there is a very early Manchester derby.

August 1- Manchester United vs Atlético Madrid August 8- PSG vs Manchester United August 12- Manchester United vs Leeds August 15- AC Milan vs Manchester United

Having played Wrexham and Rosenborg in their first two games, the level of competition will rise significantly for Manchester United in the coming weeks.

There is the final whistle and Manchester United have cruised to a 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Norway. Goals from Lacey, Zirkzee, Devaney, Amass and Williams have seen Michael Carrick’s men ease to victory. A pretty one-sided game.

The first yellow card of the game is given very late on as Devaney is booked for a high boot.

A late change for Rosenborg as Hald-Hernes replaces Borgersen.

The visitors have dominated this game and they now have their fifth goal. It is created by great work from Kamason on the right side of the box before he squares it to Williams, who has the easiest of tap-ins at the far post.

Other than a few short periods in this game, Rosenborg have looked poor. They may be midway through their league season but you can see why they are down in 10th in the Norwegian top flight with just four wins from their opening 13 league games.

You would expect that Michael Carrick will be very keen to see his side keep a clean sheet.

Manchester United have their fourth of the evening. Kamason is found making an overlapping run on the right side of the box and his cross fired towards the back post is tapped in by Amass. That was a goal assisted by one full-back and scored by the other.

Good work from Soboczynski results in Rosenborg winning a corner out on the left. They take it short before a shot is hit from the edge of the box straight down the throat of Vitek.

Rosenborg hit the post. Manchester United should probably have been given a free-kick in the build-up as Soboczynski appeared to push Devaney over but play goes on. The ball comes to E Ceide at the far post but his effort strikes the outside of the post.

Just a few minutes after making a raft of changes, Manchester United have their third goal of the evening. Rosenborg fail to clear a corner from the right and the ball falls to Devaney on the six-yard box. He takes one touch before firing into the top of the net.

Bearing in mind Rosenborg are in the middle of their league season, this has been an encouraging showing so far from United. Joshua Zirkzee has been lively. He’s still more likely to leave than stay at Old Trafford this summer but performances like this won’t hamper his value. He set up Shea Lacey for his goal with a good pass after again dropping deep into space and he’s taken that goal to give United a 2-0 lead quite brilliantly. Patrick Dorgu has been a threat and Mason Mount has dovetailed well in central midfield with new signing Andrey Santos.

Both sides are going to make a raft of changes on the hour mark, with the rest of the Manchester United starting XI being changed other than Vitek in goal.

Santos brings down Borgersen not far outside the Manchester United penalty area to give Rosenborg a decent opportunity. It is a pretty decent effort from E Ceide that goes just wide of Vitek’s right post.

The visitors have not been great since the break but they have their second and it is a great solo goal from Zirkzee. Lacey, out on the left touchline, squares it for Zirkzee, who takes the ball towards the Rosenborg penalty area. He fakes a shot, which takes numerous Rosenborg defenders out of the equation as they slide past. He then sits down the Rosenborg keeper before slotting into an empty net. A fine goal from Zirkzee.

Soboczynski has his second chance since coming on at the break after good work from E Ceide down the left but the former’s effort goes wide.

That is a really poor decision from the linesman. Duris was played in behind the Manchester United defence and thought he was through for a one-on-one chance but the offside flag goes up. However, replays prove that Duris was clearly being played onside by Amass, who has looked shaky since coming on at the break.

Zirkzee receives a pass from Dorgu on the D and takes one touch before shooting. His effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which Wahlstedt slightly unconvincingly punches away.

That is a very good chance for Rosenborg to equalise early in this second half. Amass and Heaven makes a mess of things deep in their own half, presenting Rosenborg with a good opportunity inside the Manchester United penalty area. Two Rosenborg substitutes combine as Soboczynski squares it for Borgersen but the latter makes a mess of it and shoots well wide from 10 yards out.

Michael Carrick has decided to make just a few changes at the break with Amass and Kamason coming on. Shaw and Maguire have gone off, which has seen Yoro move inside from right-back to centre-back.

Our first goalscorer of pre-season = Shea Lacey! 💎 pic.twitter.com/AyFOWNh5Fi

With no delays, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Lacey’s goal. Expect a raft of chnages at the break.

As this half has worn on, Manchester United’s dominance has only increased.

Mbeumo appeared to be racing through one-on-one but Mortensen just about gets back to outmuscle Mbeumo and allow the ball to go back to his keeper. There were a few appeals for a foul by Mortensen but that challenge was just about fine.

Other than those early stages, Manchester United have dominated the rest of this first half and are pressing for a second. For the second time in the half, they strike the frame of the goal. Mbeumo clips in a cross from the right into the Rosenborg penalty area and it picks out the head of Yoro. However, from eight yards out, the Frenchman’s header comes back off the bar.

Moments after they hit the frame of the goal, Michael Carrick’s side take the lead. Zirkzee picks up the ball inside his own half and, from the halfway line, feeds a pass into the on-running Lacey. Dorgu wants Lacey to play the ball across to him at the back post but the latter opts against it. Instead, just inside the Rosenborg penalty area, he cuts onto his preferred left foot and curls one into the far corner. A good finish from Lacey.

Just as I was saying that both sides were lacking a cutting edge in the final third, Manchester United are inches away from taking the lead as they strike the post. Santos feeds a delicate pass into the path of Dorgu on the left side of the box. Dorgu strikes his effort powerfully but it comes off the outside of the far post.

Both sides have lacked a cutting edge when they get into the opposition final third, hence why there has not been a plethora of good chances.

Mbeumo beats his man down Manchester United’s right and cuts it back to Mount on the edge of the Rosenborg penalty area. Mount hits it first time but his shot is blocked and spins behind for a corner. It is Manchester United’s first of the game but it is headed away.

That was nearly the moment for Rosenborg to take the lead. Pereira’s cross from the left-hand side of the box takes a deflection and nearly ends up at the feet of Chiakha at the back post but it is just out of his reach.

Rosenborg looked the sharper in the early exchanges but Manchester United are growing into the game and starting to gain more control.

Manchester United create their first opening of the game. Rosenborg poorly five the ball away deep inside their half and immediately Zirkzee plays it into the path of Mbeumo, whose shot from the right side of the box is saved by Rosenborg keeper Wahlstedt, who initially spilt the shot but gathered at the second attempt.

Mount trips Sahsah just outside the Manchester United penalty area, which will give Rosenborg a good shot to take an early lead. Rosenborg look a little sharper unsurprisingly in these early stages.

The Rosenborg captain Selnaes takes but hits it straight into the wall.

With Rosenborg in the midst of their season and Manchester United just in their second pre-season game, you would expect the hosts to have more rhythm and flow in their game.

Manchester United to appear to be lining up with a back four, with Yoro starting at right-back rather than his more customary centre-back position.

We are under way in Norway. Rosenborg are playing in white, with Manchester United in blue.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Harry Maguire leading Manchester United out, and we are getting closer to kick-off in Norway.

Rosenborg: Wahlstedt, Mortensen, Singsdal Volden, Nemcik, Pereira; Bomholt, Selnaes, Fossum, Sunde, Chiakha, Sahsah.Substitutes: Sandberg, Amdam, M. Ceide, Rosten, Witry, Dahl, Hald-Hernes, Slordal, Hedman, Borgersen, Bakke, E. Ceide, Duris, Soboczynski.

Manchester United: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

It’s a good opportunity for Shea Lacey tonight. He’s expected to be deployed in the hole in behind Joshua Zirkzee. A talented, highly technical footballer with a good left foot, he’ll be wanting to make the most of the chance. Another opportunity for Mason Mount to stake a claim in one of the two deeper midfield positions next to new signing Andrey Santos. Big season ahead for Mount.

INS:Andrey Santos ⇠ Chelsea, £48mYouri Tielemans ⇠ Aston Villa, £36mKarl Darlow ⇠ Leeds, FreeTynan Thompson ⇠ Tottenham, £4m

OUTS:Casemiro ⇢ Inter Miami, FreeRasmus Hojlund ⇢ Napoli, £38mJadon Sancho, FreeTyrell Malacia, Free

Forward JJ Gabriel, who does not turn 16 until October, is on the bench for Manchester United this evening. The 15-year-old has represented England at U15, U16 and U17 level. He won the inaugural Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season award for the 2025/26 campaign.

Starting XI: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire (captain), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J.Fletcher, T.Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

Dagens 11 utvalgte 🖤🤍Avspark er klokken 18.00 🏟️ pic.twitter.com/LuZrojJM4l

Bring on United! 🫡Watch Rosenborg v United LIVE on MUTV, with build-up starting at 16:00 BST 📲

Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.

Massimiliano Allegri, tecnico del Napoli, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni a Sport TV a margine della sconfitta in Champions subita per 4-1 contro il Porto di Francesco Farioli. #2252. Blackburn Rovers vs West Ham predictions: Scott Parker backed for first win in ‘entertaining contest’

Blackburn Rovers head into Saturday’s clash with West Ham sitting 14th in the Championship table. Tony Mowbray’s side have endured an inconsistent start to the campaign, collecting 18 points from 14 games, with five wins, three draws and six defeats leaving them just outside the Championship play-off picture.

Rovers have shown signs of their attacking potential, though, beating Wrexham 2-0 at Ewood Park two weeks ago. Andri Gudjohnsen scored both goals in that victory, taking his league tally to nine and accounting for almost half of Blackburn’s goals this season.

West Ham arrive currently 8th in the Championship with 22 points and have been among the more prolific sides in the league, averaging more than 2.5 goals per game. Scott Parker, appointed following Nuno Espirito Santo’s departure, will be looking for a response after a disappointing result last time out.

WHUFC went three goals down against Cardiff City before eventually rescuing a 3-3 draw. Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman were all on target in South Wales, but Parker will be concerned by his side’s defensive shortcomings as they prepare for another difficult away assignment.

“Blackburn Rovers have shown enough attacking quality to suggest they can cause West Ham problems, particularly with Gudjohnsen enjoying an excellent run in front of goal. The Icelandic striker has become an important figure for Mowbray, while Todd Cantwell’s creativity gives the hosts another route to hurting their opponents.

“However, West Ham possess considerably more individual quality and should have enough firepower to trouble Rovers’ defence. Jarrod Bowen has been particularly influential, registering seven goals and seven assists in 14 league appearances.

“The visitors will need to improve defensively after their collapse against Cardiff, but their attacking options should ultimately make the difference. Blackburn can contribute to an entertaining contest at Ewood Park, although I expect Parker’s side to come away with all three points.”

“Blackburn Rovers have had some tough games of late. They were narrowly beaten by a great West Brom side, thrashed by Swansea City, and then hard done by to lose to Stoke City after a very soft disallowed goal late on.

“I think Rovers are going to see form come and go this season, largely because their squad isn’t very deep and relies on the form and availability of key figures like Andri Gudjohnsen, Todd Cantwell and Sam Morsy. Despite this, they’re dangerous with their front-footed play under Tony Mowbray and have had some good results at home.

“West Ham will be one to keep an eye on this weekend though. They will have had a couple of days to work under Scott Parker on the training ground after that great comeback draw at Cardiff City.

“We’ll get a better idea of what to expect from WHUFC as they settle into Parker’s management. I do think they have the talent to win the midfield battle though, and with quality players like Jarrod Bowen, I can see them creating the chances to win this one.”

#2251. Ronaldo, ritiro dal Portogallo: «È arrivato il momento»

Jorge Jesus aveva riaperto le porte al numero 7: resta l’ipotesi di un ultimo saluto nella prossima pausa.

Secondo quanto riportato da Onefootball, Cristiano Ronaldo dice addio alla Nazionale portoghese. L’annuncio del ritiro è arrivato attraverso un video pubblicato sul suo profilo Instagram, nel quale ha ripercorso gli oltre vent’anni trascorsi con la maglia del Portogallo.

La decisione segue di poche settimane quella, definita storica, del suo rivale Lionel Messi. Per Ronaldo si chiude un percorso con la Nazionale segnato da 146 gol in 234 partite.

Nel video, l’ex giocatore del Real Madrid ripercorre il tempo trascorso a rappresentare il proprio Paese. «È arrivato il momento», è la frase attribuita a Ronaldo in un titolo collegato all’annuncio.

Un altro titolo dedicato al ritiro riporta le parole «Consegno la 7 della Nazionale dopo 23 anni». Il riferimento è alla maglia numero 7 indossata da Cristiano con il Portogallo.

I 146 gol in 234 presenze hanno accompagnato il Portogallo alla conquista di un Europeo e di due Nations League. Nel racconto di Onefootball, resta il rammarico per il Mondiale: Ronaldo ha partecipato a sei edizioni senza riuscire a vincerlo.

L’addio alla Nazionale arriva dunque dopo oltre due decenni e dopo i successi ottenuti con la selezione portoghese, ma senza il titolo mondiale.

#2249. ‘Catalyst’ victory can inspire Wrexham to a result in Wolves clash: Predictions

Wrexham beat league leaders Middlesbrough at home on Wednesday night. George Thomason and Ollie Rathbone scored two late goals for the Welsh outfit as they returned to winning ways in impressive fashion.

The Red Dragons are sat in 16th place in the Championship table after their first 14 fixtures and they have made a slow start to the season. They are only six points off the play-offs now behind West Ham in 8th position.

As for Wolves, they came from behind away at Bristol City last time out to win 2-1. Newcastle United loan man Sean Neave scored two second-half goals to earn WWFC an important three points at Ashton Gate against the Robins.

Cesar Peixoto‘s men have now risen into 2nd in the division behind Middlesbrough ahead of Birmingham City. The Midlands club were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with West Ham and Burnley.

“Wrexham’s win over Middlesbrough was much needed and has eased some pressure off Phil Parkinson. It has been a tough season for the Red Dragons so far and they will be eager to hit some form now.

“The Welsh side haven’t scored enough goals in this campaign and are lacking a cutting edge. In fact, only six teams have scored less than them in the Championship so far.

“Wolves found a way to win at Bristol City which is a good sign for a team eyeing automatic promotion. WWFC are now unbeaten in their last five games since their home defeat to Bolton Wanderers last month.

“Cesar Peixoto’s squad is littered with Premier League quality and they will fancy their chances in North Wales. However, I think it may end a high scoring draw with the hosts seemingly back on track now.”

“Wrexham produced arguably their best performance of the season to beat Middlesbrough on Wednesday night. That has to be a catalyst for Phil Parkinson if he’s to hold onto his job and if the Red Dragons are to push up the Championship table.

“Another tricky game awaits here with Wolves unbeaten in five, but another home match marks a chance for the North Welsh side to build some momentum and head into the break on a high.

“Wolves are in high spirits themselves though. They’ve responded to poor form with a five-game unbeaten run, the most recent being an impressive comeback win thanks to a Sean Neave brace. That will be a real confidence boost for the young striker as well, as he looks to step up to the senior game and deliver while Wanderers star Raul Jimenez is out.

“This is a tough one to call, as Wrexham are capable of picking up another win if they play like they did on Wednesday. However, I can’t see Wolves losing, so I’ll say this ends level.”

#2248. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

The referee brings this contest to a close and it finishes a goal apiece at Gateshead International Stadium. Not the result Howe was hoping for, but he can at least find some comfort in a positive showing from new signing Steur in the heart of midfield.

Newcastle ended up with 76 per cent of the ball and created three ‘big chances’ but lacked the cutting edge in the final third to make that dominance tell. Credit must go to Gateshead who defended resolutely and took their best chance of the match.

The hosts have near enough seven bodies in their back line and Newcastle are struggling to find a way through.

Newcastle have five minutes, plus added time, to grab a go-ahead goal. Plenty of industry on show from the youngsters who have come on, but the play has largely been restricted to a midfield slug-fest in the last minutes.

Triple substitution from Howe. Hall, Ramsey and Willock make way for Salia, Munda and Charlton.

Gateshead 1 Newcastle 1 (OG) Hall’s cross from the left in turned by Williams. Newcastle had been turning the screw as Gateshead dropped deeper and deeper.

Sanusi and Park replace Murphy and Barnes.

There is the first yellow card of the match. Home lands an overzealous challenge on Willock in the centre of the pitch and receives a booking for his troubles.

Ferreira is then played into the left channel and unleashes a shot which is turned behind for a corner by Desbois, who has been awesome this afternoon.

Jaouen, Miley and Ferreira replace Pope, Shahar and Neave.

Gateshead are sitting deeper meaning that their penalty area is often getting quite congested.

There are opportunities for the hosts to counter, though, and Boatswain has the chance to play in Telford but severely overhits the through-ball.

A note on Steur... He’s completed 65 of his 68 attempted passes so far. That’s 96 per cent. Impressive stuff.

Hall falls on to the ball under pressure on the byline. The referee awards a free-kick to Gateshead and Hall protests his case. Just not happening for the left-back, who has been given the licence to get forward.

Murphy switches wings to create an overload with Barnes down the left and flashes a cross into the box which is dealt with by Gateshead. Newcastle need more invention like that if they are to break down this stubborn Gateshead side.

Chance for Newcastle! Steur releases Barnes into the left channel and he plays the ball across goal but just in front of Neave who had the freedom of Tyneside at the back post. Desbois is called into action moments later, punching the ball clear after some pinball in the box.

Steur shifts the ball on to his left foot and has a go from 25 yards out, firing the ball high and wide. Good intent, though.

Ramsey is dropping in to receive the ball to feet. His average position in the first half was significantly more withdrawn than Willock’s, and Howe will surely look to get him further up the pitch to affect play in the final third in the second period.

An immediate chance for the hosts’ front man Boatswain at the start of the second half. The ball just gets away from him.

Newcastle go into the break a goal down. There have been chances for the visitors, who dominated the ball in that first period. Expect changes at the interval.

Gateshead’s goal came against the run of play and was there first shot on target. It’s not great from Fabian Schar, who conceded the free kick competing for a long ball down the middle and Nick Pope was a little slow off his line to smother the shot too.

Gateshead 1 Newcastle 0 (Supyk) Gateshead win a free-kick 25 yards out, just to the right of the D. Chadwick’s initial effort ricochets through the wall and new signing Supyk is first on to the scene to prod the ball beyond Pope. A calamity at the back for Howe’s side!

Neave comes close to opening the scoring, firing an effort across the face of goal that goes behind for a corner.

Hall then gets a shot away from the edge of the box, but cannot keep his half-volley down and the ball sails over the bar.

Newcastle look most dangerous when Schar steps up and punches in those line-breaking passes. Gateshead defending resolutely, though, keeping things compact across the backline.

Murphy earns his side a free-kick down the right. He delivers the ball himself, with the box loaded with Schar and Murphy, and the former steals in to the near post but cannot quite stoop down low enough to get a meaningful contact on the ball. Desbois gathers without fuss.

Newcastle have won a glut of corners down their left, all of which have been taken short. The latest is played out to Steur who rains in a cross which is claimed by the goalkeeper.

Sean Steur looks like a player... some really nice touches from the young Dutchman. He is always looking to make a progressive pass and has been a real bright spark. Newcastle have dominated the game. As you would expect against opposition four divisions below them

Another tidy involvement from Steur, who disguises a pass to Ramsey on the edge of the box. The ball is worked into the path of Murphy and deflects out for a corner. The former Ajax midfielder is growing in confidence.

Hall puts in another ball from the left, this time to the back post, where the ball is headed away by Ferguson.

New signing Steur is starting to creep forward, carrying the ball nicely and picking it back up in the right channel. He stands a cross up to the near post but Murphy’s header is dealt with by Desbois.

Hall works a yard of space in a dangerous area down the left moments later, but the ball ricochets back off him and out for goal-kick.

Hall punches in a lovely ball down the line for Barnes to run on to, but the move is snuffed out by Robinson.

It does seem strange that this game has not sold out. There are thought to be about 7,000 fans inside the stadium, which once had a capacity of more than 11,000 when it was one of the country’s premier athletics venues. They even used to have Diamond League events here not so long ago.

But the capacity has been steadily reduced for safety reasons and it is rarely used for anything other than local athletic events and Gateshead FC games.

There were officially only 50 tickets left for sale a few minutes before kick-off, but there are lots of empty seats.

Chadwick lofts a tidy cross in from the left, but Boatswain’s header drifts wide of the mark. The chance came off a decent spell of possession from Cattermole’s side, the most fluent they have been in this match so far.

Ramsey regains possession high up the pitch and releases Barnes who plays in Murphy, but the Newcastle forward mistimes his run and the linesman’s flag goes up. A promising counter.

Ramsey is brought down on the edge of the box as he tries to break free and the referee awards a free-kick. There are a few contenders to take it (Schar, Barnes, Hall) but in the end it is Barnes who gets a shot away, but his curled effort flies just wide of the mark.

Another weighted ball over the top from Schar puts Anifowose under pressure in the left channel but his ball across the face of goal is cleared to safety by a team-mate.

Newcastle circulating the ball in front of Gateshead’s first line of pressure. The hosts regain possession but struggle to find a way through Newcastle’s midfield.

Schar getting a few early touches as he makes his return from injury. He plays a long, raking diagonal out to Barnes who cannot quite get past his man.

Neave tests Desbois with a well-struck effort off the next phase of play.

The officials and both sets of players line up behind a banner with the message ‘Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan’. Newcastle are in their new navy-blue away shirt, with Gateshead in their home white-and-black kit. A minute’s silence is then observed immaculately.

The tributes left in honour of Kevin Keegan outside St James’ Park is a sight to behold, with flowers, shirts and scarves covering the ground and steps in the south-west corner. It is a very moving thing to behold as people come to pay their respects to the Newcastle legend.

There will also be a minute’s silence before today’s game against Gateshead.

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

💬 "What a game for [the players] to go & play."Lee Cattermole talks tomorrow's game against @NUFC at the GIS ⤵️📺👉 https://t.co/DGuJRosJ2K pic.twitter.com/rccs5FzhG6

A classic first-game-of-pre-season vibe to Newcastle’s team sheet as established stars rub shoulders with youngsters from the academy.

Only one of their four summer signings, former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur, starts the game and there will be a lot of interest in the 18-year-old. The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Gateshead lost manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle at the end of last season and are now managed by former Sunderland and Middlesbrough midfielder Lee Cattermole.
