#2173. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#2172. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#2171. Hearts learn match officials for FC Thun and Falkirk double-header

Officials have been confirmed for Heart of Midlothian's upcoming clashes with FC Thun and Falkirk.

Hearts travel to Switzerland to face Thun at the Visana Stadion in the Conference League before returning to Premiership action against Falkirk at Tynecastle on Sunday.

Cypriot referee Kyriakos Athanasiou will take charge of the European encounter. He will be assisted by Marios Kalogirou and Kyriakos Sokratous, with Chrysovalantis Theouli appointed as the fourth official. Marios Christoforou will be on VAR duty, assisted by Dimitris Solomou.

Thursday's game is set to be Athanasiou’s first appointment involving Hearts. His previous European record also includes Conference League matches.

Hearts will then turn their attention back to domestic action when Falkirk visit Tynecastle on Sunday, November 8, for a 3pm kick-off.

Matthew MacDermid has been appointed as referee, with Chris Rae and Colin Drummond running the lines. Sean Murdoch will be the fourth official, while Steven McLean is on VAR duty and Gary Hilland will assist him.

MacDermid has previous experience of Hearts matches. He took charge of their 2-2 Premiership draw away to St Mirren in October 2025 before refereeing their 3-1 home victory over Motherwell in April.

#2170. Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 penalties): Gunners knocked out of Carabao Cup as Max Dowman is sent off

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal suffered a stunning Carabao Cup exit. They lost on penalties to League Two side Fleetwood Town 5-3 in the fourth round at Highbury Stadium. A 1-1 draw meant Arsenal had to go to penalties. Teenager Max Dowman was sent off five minutes from the end of the game.

Fleetwood, in 18th place in League Two, took an early lead, but Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal of the season to bring them level. However, neither team could find a winning goal. Fleetwood held their composure to win the penalty shootout after Bruno Guimaraes missed his spot-kick. The game was also paused for two minutes due to a drone flying around the ground.

Despite a heavy rotation by Mikel Arteta, Kai Havertz, Gyokeres, Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Jurrien Timber all started. Martin Odegaard and Ben White were brought on during the half-time break, followed by Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Eberechi Eze. But overall the Evening Standard said Arsenal put in an “incredibly bad performance” over the course of the 90 minutes.

Dowman, 16, had been among Arsenal’s better players, creating chances for Havertz and Timber with dangerous crosses. He was shown a straight red card after reacting angrily to a heavy challenge from Harrison Neal and kicking out at the defender, though the force was minimal. It was his second red card this month, after a dismissal for the England Under-19s.

As Dowman walked off, Arteta was seen leaning towards him and delivering furious words. Asked what he said, the Arsenal manager told BBC Radio 5 Live it was “something that we discussed already before the match”. Suggesting the teenager had been warned to expect rough treatment. Arteta said he had not seen the red card back and that the referee’s decision stood. Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson was critical of how the Arsenal boss reacted to Dowman.

Arteta congratulated Fleetwood Town on the atmosphere they created. He said he could not fault his players’ attitude and intensity, with 11 men or 10. “When we create the volume of shots and chances we did, you have to score three, four or five,” he said. He added that even with ten men Arsenal had three big chances.

He called the unpredictability of cup football part of English football’s history, saying Arsenal were “extremely sad” to be on the wrong side of it.

Several squad members were absent. Riccardo Calafiori was out, and Noni Madueke had an ankle problem. Declan Rice was substituted in the previous game because of a concern.

Arsenal’s Carabao Cup dream of a first League Cup win since 1993 is over. Attention now turns to a huge Premier League trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday. Fleetwood, meanwhile, can celebrate a famous giant-killing and wait for the quarter-final draw.

#2169. Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Champions League preview, team news and how to watch

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women face Benfica at Meadow Park tonight, and as they prepare to enter a tough clash in the UEFA Women’s Champions League, head coach Renée Slegers has called for ‘grit and fight’ from her players. The match kicks off at 8pm in Borehamwood and will be available to watch live on Disney+ for UK fans.

Arsenal come into the match on the back of a 2-1 north London derby win at Tottenham. The team sit fifth in the European league with four points, having won 1-0 at home against HB Koge and drawn 2-2 at Paris FC. Benfica are currently sitting in tenth place but will overtake them if they win.

Slegers said the main factor behind Arsenal’s derby win was intensity. “It was a really intense game. We had to fight for it. We scored first, and we came back, so that’s what makes me really proud. Now we have to make sure we follow that up,” she said at London Colney on Tuesday.

Kim Little returns to the squad. Slegers confirmed that Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang will not be back in time, while Frida Maanum is progressing, but the game comes too soon.

Taylor Hinds was a player of the match contender at Tottenham, playing a full 90 minutes for only the second time this season. Alongside Steph Catley, she linked up well on the left. Slegers has not named the same starting XI in back-to-back games this season, though, and said Arsenal will need “sharpness, quality and injections” late on against Benfica.

The referee is Ivana Projkovska of North Macedonia, who was among the officials for the 2025 Champions League final, when Arsenal beat Barcelona 1-0 in Lisbon.

Benfica have won all four of their Campeonato Nacional Feminino games as they look to retain their title, conceding once, in Saturday’s 4-1 win over Sporting CP. In Europe, Ivan Baptista’s side won 2-1 at Juventus before losing 3-0 at home to Bayern Munich. They have made more interceptions than any other team in this season’s competition, with 33, while Arsenal have made only 13.

Slegers expects a physical, compact opponent, similar in some ways to the derby, though with some changes in personnel since last season, when Arsenal won 2-0 at the Estadio da Luz through Beth Mead and Alessia Russo. Baptista said being seen as favourites means little to him and that his team will cause Arsenal difficulties again.

The record favours the hosts. Arsenal have won 10 of their last 13 home league-phase games in the competition, including the last three, while Benfica have won only three of their last 15 away matches in the tournament.

Slegers admitted the domestic start has been tough but said it is too early to judge and that Arsenal are proud to be back on the Champions League stage. Last season they finished fifth in the league phase before reaching the semi-finals.

#2168. AC Milan 3-1 Inter: Moreira inspires commanding fourth straight derby win

AC Milan recorded a huge win in the derby against Inter, scoring three times in the first half to secure a 3-1 win.

It did not take long for Milan to go in front, with Christian Pulisic heading in a cross from Diego Moreira. Then, just a few minutes later, Adrien Rabiot was on hand to fire in a corner first time and make it a two-goal lead.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Alessandro Bastoni scored from a corner to make it a one-goal lead once again, but then Moreira’s free-kick re-established the two-goal lead and that would be enough to see the Rossoneri through to the end of the game.

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan in the derby and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that lost to Bologna on Wednesday night, with Mario Gila, Sankhoun Diawara, Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all getting the nod.

Inside four minutes, Milan took the lead and it was the derby talisman Christian Pulisic who struck once again. It was quite a simple move down the right side in the end, with Diego Moreira checking back inside onto his left foot and whipped in a simply perfect cross for Pulisic to nod in from a few yards out.

Then, just a few minutes later, Milan doubled their advantage from a set-piece after another good spell of pressure. A low delivery from Moreira found the run of Rabiot towards the near post, who somehow managed to divert it in via the far post to make it 2-0.

Midway through the first half, Inter got themselves back into the game through a dead ball of their own. A corner was flicked on at the near post towards Bastoni, who was on hand to nod in from a few yards with the Milan defenders rooted.

Inter assumed the ascendancy after the goal, and they twice threatened in quick succession shortly after their first goal. Calhanoglu had a shot tipped over from the edge of the box, then another flicked header from a corner drew a desperate reaction save from Maignan.

Milan continued to give their city rivals opportunities to try and make it a brand new game. A silly foul by Pavlovic on Spence drew a free-kick just off the right edge of the box, though the eventual shot from Diouf was grasped by Maignan.

Just over 10 minutes before the break, Inter had another chance to draw themselves level. A cross from the left was not cut out by Koni De Winter, and the ball fells to Spence who fired with his left foot, but the Frenchman makes a brilliant reaction save to deflect the shot out for a corner.

Just two minutes before the break, Milan restored their two-goal advantage thanks to a quite simply beautiful free-kick from Diego Moreira. After getting two assists to his name already on the night, he turned scorer with a fantastic attempt that was up and over the wall, dipping just enough to land inside the near right post.

Ten minutes into the second half, Inter had the first big opening and it fell to their recent danger man Carlos Augusto. A cross to the far post wasn’t tracked by anyone and the wing-back ghosted in at the far post, heading it wide from about a yard off the ground.

With 25 minutes left, a corner this time for Milan: Modric’s cross from the left finds Rabiot at the near post, who tries to head it in, but his connection was poor and the ball went straight out.

In the 75th minute, it looked like the game was going to be on once again when the referee gave a penalty for what he adjudged to be a handball on Mario Gila. The replays show that the cross struck his midriff, and therefore the penalty was overturned to be a corner.

With the game settled into a rhythm of attack versus defence, Amorim chose to make a double change with eight minutes to go. Pulisic and Diawara were the ones who came off, with Alphadjo Cisse and Davide Bartesaghi the ones to come on.

In the penultimate minute of added time, a double sub came from Amorim. Ramos and Moreira came off, Filippo Terracciano and Omari Hutchinson came on.

Alphadjo Cisse came on inside the final minutes and immediately came close to scoring. The Italian forward tried a curling shot from outside the area, but Martinez saved well to put it out for a corner, keeping it 3-1.

#2167. Arsenal injury news: Rice, Madueke and Calafiori concerns ahead of Liverpool clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal injury news has been in the headlines ahead of their visit to Anfield. Mikel Arteta confirmed Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori were all sidelined for their Carabao Cup clash against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.

The Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties following their 1-1 draw at Highbury Stadium. Arsenal will face Liverpool at 4.30pm on Sunday. They have a number of injury concerns, plus a suspended teenager to deal with.

When questioned if the three players had just been rested, Arteta replied that Calafiori was unavailable. Madueke had issues with his ankle and Rice was “feeling something on the previous day”, making visible the reason why he has been substituted.

Martin Zubimendi replaced Rice in Saturday’s game when he substituted the player in the 80th minute of the game versus Everton due to Rice grabbing his hamstring. Madueke played till the end of the game. However, he was not spotted in training Monday, and Arteta did not provide any estimation for his return.

Calafiori appears to be in a better place. After being described as having a ‘slight issue’ by Arteta following the Everton game. DaveOCKOP reports that the defender is expected to be available against Anfield.

Winger Christos Tzolis has also been ruled out for five games with a hamstring injury. We’re likely to get an update on how all three are feeling going into the game from Arteta’s pre-match press conference.

Bukayo Saka is still sidelined with a quadriceps injury picked up against Bayern Munich in the Champions League. Arteta said the injury will take “weeks” to recover from, as he needs another scan due to fluid around the area. William Saliba has not played this season due to a back issue and is unlikely to return until December.

Arsenal’s problems were deepened at Highbury. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put Fleetwood ahead in the 21st minute. Viktor Gyokeres equalised five minutes after the restart, shortly after captain Martin Odegaard came on at half-time. Max Dowman was then sent off in the 85th minute for kicking out at Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal.

The 16-year-old will serve a three-match ban, reportedly covering the trip to Liverpool, the home game against Hull and the visit to Newcastle.

Fleetwood scored all five penalties. Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Gyokeres converted for Arsenal. Goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved Bruno Guimaraes’ effort, and 19-year-old defender Conor Haughey scored the winner. It was reportedly the first time the reigning top-flight champions have lost a League Cup tie to a fourth-tier side. There’s 84 places separating the clubs.

Arteta said the result was not down to attitude. “I’m sad, we’re all sad,” he said.

#2166. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#2165. Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Alessia Russo Hat-Trick Fires Arsenal Women to 3-0 Champions League Win Over Benfica

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Arsenal Women continued their unbeaten start to the UEFA Women’s Champions League league phase with a convincing 3-0 victory over Benfica at Mangata Developments Stadium on Wednesday night.

Alessia Russo hit a hat trick to claim the spoils and become the top scorer in English Women’s Champions League history. The England international opened the scoring before the break and added two more after the interval.

Despite controlling much of the game Arsenal’s attacking play was stymied by the determined Benfica defence and the inspired Lena Pauels in goal. The German made some stunning saves before Russo finally found a way through.

Arsenal came out firing after their win in the North London derby. Olivia Smith put Pauels under pressure after just 65 seconds.

She made another save soon after as the hosts took control of the game and created a number of great chances.

Geraldine Reuteler made her first start for Arsenal and nearly picked out Smith with a dangerous delivery into the penalty area. Russo also saw an effort blocked following a well-worked set piece.

Georgia Stanway came closest to breaking the deadlock during the opening half-hour. The midfielder escaped her marker before sending a powerful shot towards the bottom corner, but Pauels reacted well to keep the score level.

The Benfica goalkeeper continued her impressive performance by denying Caitlin Foord from the resulting corner.

Benfica gradually grew into the contest and threatened through Froya Dorsin, who wasted an opportunity by firing over the crossbar. The visitors created further pressure before Arsenal regained control.

Russo sent an effort narrowly wide before Smith forced another save from Pauels.

However, Arsenal finally broke through five minutes before half-time. Foord supplied a clever pass into Russo, who placed a precise finish against the far post and into the net.

Arsenal kept their forward momentum going into the second half and nearly extended their lead.

Kyra Cooney-Cross found an excellent ball over the top for Foord but was thwarted by a vital challenge from Catarina Amado.

Foord continued to pose a threat and got on the end of a cross from Ona Batlle at the back post. She powered a header across the goal, but Benfica cleared it in time to stop Russo getting on the end of it.

Smith then tested Pauels again with a deflected effort, but the goalkeeper could not prevent Arsenal from scoring their second.

Russo rose to meet Steph Catley’s corner and headed home to extend the hosts’ lead. The goal was her 22nd in the competition, making her the leading English goalscorer in UEFA Women’s Champions League history.

Benfica responded with a dangerous effort from Andreia Norton, forcing Misa Rodriguez into a good save at her near post.

Arsenal quickly threatened on the counter-attack, with Reuteler rounding Pauels before Diana Gomes cleared her effort off the line.

Pauels kept the game alive for Benfica but made a fantastic save to keep out Smith’s powerful strike in the 15th minute.

But Arsenal finally won the game after Amado brought down Foord inside the penalty box.

Russo stepped up and confidently converted from 12 yards to complete her hat-trick and take her Champions League tally to 23 goals.

Foord thought she had added a fourth during stoppage time, but the officials ruled out her effort for offside.

The result means Arsenal remain undefeated in the league phase of the tournament and also highlights the importance of Russo to the club’s European campaign.

They return to Women’s Super League action on Sunday, November 1, when they play Aston Villa at Emirates Stadium before facing Liverpool. On November 12 they head to Spain to face defending European champions Barcelona.

#2164. Hibs learn match officials for Saturday evening Aberdeen showdown

Officials have been confirmed for Hibernian’s Premiership trip to Aberdeen.

Hibs travel to Pittodrie on Saturday, November 7, with the league clash scheduled for a 5.45pm kick-off.

Duncan Nicolson has been appointed as the man in the middle, with Graeme Stewart and Christopher Gentles running the lines. Jamie Wilkie will be the fourth official, while Kevin Clancy is on VAR duty with Grant Irvine assisting.

It will not be Nicolson’s first involvement with Hibs this season. He took charge of their 1-0 League Cup victory over Partick Thistle at Easter Road in August.

Nicolson also refereed one Hibs match during the 2025/26 season, when the Easter Road side suffered a 2-0 Premiership defeat away to Motherwell in November. That encounter saw one red card as Motherwell claimed all three points at Fir Park.

Saturday’s appointment will therefore be Nicolson’s third Hibs match across the last two seasons.

The Aberdeen encounter will be Hibernian’s 12th Premiership fixture of the 2026/27 campaign.

#2163. Arsenal Max Dowman Red Card Appeal Faces Rejection, Says Dermot Gallagher

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Former Premier League official Dermot Gallagher has said he thinks Arsenal won’t be successful in their appeal against Max Dowman’s red card in their Carabao Cup loss to Fleetwood Town.

The 16-year-old Arsenal winger was shown a red card for violent conduct after lashing out at Harrison Neal after a strong challenge from the Fleetwood defender. The Gunners then lost the fourth-round tie on penalties.

Arsenal are appealing the sending off of Max Dowman. They need to have their paperwork in by 1pm today (Thursday). They will be hoping to get a decision before their Premier League game against Liverpool on Sunday.

But Gallagher does not think they will be successful in their appeal as he believes there was clear intent from Dowman.

“I think it was a red card for the actions of the teenager,” Gallagher said.

He also thinks the referee should have given Arsenal a free kick as well as booking Neal for his challenge on Dowman.

Gallagher told Sky Sports News that the attitude of Dowman could be an issue for Arsenal in their red card appeal.

“I think he went out of his way to kick his leg up. It makes it difficult to overturn the decision,” Gallagher said.

“He’s got more of an aggressive reaction than what Cole Palmer had recently with Mateus Fernandes.”

But Gallagher was critical of the challenge made by Neal on the Arsenal youngster. He said that while Fleetwood’s defender did win the ball back, he didn’t think the challenge was made with enough consideration for Dowman’s safety.

“I think he should have got a free-kick and a yellow card,” he added.

The debate leaves Arsenal facing a difficult decision ahead of their Premier League fixture against Liverpool. If the appeal fails, Dowman’s dismissal will stand.

Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson said he disagreed with Gallagher’s comments, saying it was a harsh red card.

“It was a classic old fashioned tackle. He (Neal) wins the ball and then follows through. I think the reaction from the players might have had something to do with the referee giving Dowman a red card.”

Merson also warned the young Gunner that he will always be a target for opposition players.

Dowman has had disciplinary problems in the past, being sent off whilst playing for England against the USA. Merson feels the youngster needs to learn to control his emotions and not get caught up in the taunts of opposition players.

The incident has also raised more questions over how Arsenal are developing one of their most promising young talents.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta also attracted criticism for his reaction to Dowman after the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town.

As the teenager walked towards the tunnel, Arteta leaned towards him and spoke to him. Merson questioned the approach, arguing that the Arsenal manager should have offered reassurance to the 16-year-old instead.

Arteta declined to reveal exactly what he told Dowman, explaining only that they had discussed the matter before the match.

The Arsenal boss also said the team had prepared for the emotional challenges they expected to face during the tie.

Jobi McAnuff similarly questioned Arteta’s response, arguing that Dowman remains young and will inevitably make mistakes as he develops.

Arsenal must now wait for the outcome of their red card appeal. With Liverpool next on the fixture list, the decision could have important implications for Arteta’s selection plans.

#2162. Arsenal predicted XI vs Liverpool: Four injury doubts as Arteta faces Anfield test

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal face a major test of their Premier League title credentials when they travel to Liverpool on Sunday, with Mikel Arteta waiting on several key players ahead of the Anfield clash.

The Gunners will be looking to bounce back after a shock defeat in the Carabao Cup midweek against Fleetwood Town. However, injuries have hampered their preparations ahead of the big clash with four players injured.

Noni Madueke, Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis are all in doubt for the game against Liverpool and could affect Arteta’s decision when selecting his team.

Saka will miss Sunday’s Premier League fixture because of a quad injury, leaving Arsenal without one of their most important attacking players.

Madueke could provide a timely boost after missing the Fleetwood defeat with an ankle problem. The injury is not believed to be serious, and Arsenal hope the winger will recover in time to face Liverpool.

The prospect of him returning is important as Max Dowman is suspended after receiving a red card against Fleetwood. Arsenal will appeal against it, but there is no guarantee that it will be decided by Sunday’s game.

Tzolis is also set to return soon. However, it is not clear whether he will be fit for the clash with Liverpool.

Arsenal have a disappointing midweek performance to overcome and need to make sure they utilise their attacking options. Both Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres struggled against Fleetwood.

Havertz had a difficult evening; however, Arteta can still include the German in one of the most important fixtures of the season.

Rice will be another major talking point heading into Arsenal’s visit to Merseyside.

The midfielder was absent for the Fleetwood game after appearing to have hamstring issues in his appearance against Everton last weekend, but there is hope that he can be in the squad on Sunday.

It would give Arteta a real boost in the midfield going up against Liverpool.

Calafiori is also a doubt. He sustained an injury in the latter stages of Arsenal’s win against Everton. The extent of the injury has not been confirmed.

If the Italian fails to recover in time, then Myles Lewis-Skelly could be brought in to play as left back. However, the Gunners will have to see how Calafiori is before they decide what backline they’ll be using.

William Saliba is also out with an injury.

Arsenal are expected to make several changes to the side that lost to Fleetwood, but Madueke and Rice have to prove their fitness.

Predicted Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz.

Doubts: Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice, Noni Madueke, Christos Tzolis.

Arsenal visit Anfield on Sunday, November 1, 2026. The game kicks off at 8pm GMT.

The game will be shown live on Sky Sports in the UK.

Arteta will have some key decisions to make ahead of the game after Saka was ruled out and a number of players are fighting to be fit. Arsenal will be hoping to put their Carabao Cup disappointment behind them and put in a better performance.

#2161. Player Ratings: AC Milan 3-1 Inter – Moreira show; De Winter responds

AC Milan clinched a massive win at San Siro to paint the city of Milan red and black. Below are the player ratings for the Rossoneri, with several high ones handed out.

After an up-and-down start to the season, Milan headed into the Derby della Madonnina knowing that a win would make all the difference. Gerry Cardinale said as much before the game and luckily, they succeeded with a 3-1 win.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Moreira (9.5 – MOTM): He’s rough around the edges sometimes, but with one fantastic goal and two very good assists in a derby, he deserves all the praise he can get. I expressed doubts about him playing on the right but tonight was his best game in that role. Really, really encouraging ahead of what’s to come.

👎 Everyone got over a 6 tonight, so there was no flop.

👔 Amorim (7): Individual brilliance was the difference-maker, BUT, it would be rude not to acknowledge some of Amorim’s moves tonight. He got the starting eleven spot on, waited with the substitutions, and gave his players good advice at the interval to avoid another push from Inter in the second half.

Maignan (8): He made a fantastic save on Spence in the first half, using his reflexes, and it’s a save that really paved the way for the win. There were other good interventions too, like the volleyball-esque clearance on Calhanoglu’s corner, and coming out to head the ball away. CAPITANO!

Gila (7): I don’t think it’s a coincidence that Milan suddenly looked much more solid with him back in the defensive four. That said, he didn’t stand out with any major interventions, but was just very good through calm passing, good positioning and marshalling. When he’s back to 100% fit, he will be even more important.

De Winter (8): He absolutely won the battle against Thuram this game and it’s not like it was an easy one either. The two had several 50-50 duels and he always came out on top. Aside from his Thuram battle, he was very good overall and deserves a high rating here.

Pavlovic (7.5): It was a bit of a roller coaster for him, but allow me to explain. He left Bastoni on the goal and simply shouldn’t have, for many reasons, and then he also missed a good chance in attack. However, the second half was brilliant with several last-ditch clearances/tackles, including a wonderful one on Barella to stop a goal. That tackle was worth everything in my opinion.

Diawara (6.5): Considering it was his first derby, and game of this calibre, we have to give him praise. He had a cautious style and it worked tonight, as he often just needed to stop his man/block the cross rather than trying to make something extraordinary with the ball. One good cross in attack for Pavlovic, which we shouldn’t forget.

Moreira (9.5 – MOTM): He’s rough around the edges sometimes, but with one fantastic goal and two very good assists in a derby, he deserves all the praise he can get. I expressed doubts about him playing on the right but tonight was his best game in that role. Really, really encouraging ahead of what’s to come.

Musah (7): He won the free-kick that Moreira converted with some smart body work. In addition to that, he was very composed (something he often struggles with) and really helped Milan get out of several tough/tight situations. One poor giveaway at the end but overall, very solid.

Modric (7.5): The veteran stayed on for the entire 90 minutes and fought until the very end. There was one sequence in the final minutes/last ten or so when he really had to scrap to get out of a tight jam, and did so successfully. What a player.

Pulisic (8): It was a great header to open the scoring for Milan, celebrating his renewal in style. The positioning is what makes him so brilliant, not just on the goal but also how he links the midfield and attack together. Could he have been even more effective on the ball? Yes, but the importance of the movement shouldn’t be played down just because it wasn’t always fireworks.

Rabiot (7.5): I’m stunned by the awareness to opt for a finish like that on the goal, but that’s why he’s such a highly-rated footballer. He was good aside from that but perhaps could have been even more effective on the ball for a higher rating. Then again, his movement and running is key.

Ramos (6.5): It feels like I say it every game, aside from the last one when he genuinely looked tired, but the running helps Milan so much in opening up space. Now, his rating is not super high here and that’s because he can still do more on the ball/in the box, but it was good.

Since all the substitutions were made from the 82nd minute onwards, I just didn’t see enough to give either of them a rating.

Bartesaghi, Jashari, Cisse, Terracciano and Hutchinson: N/A

Amorim (7): Individual brilliance was the difference-maker, BUT, it would be rude not to acknowledge some of Amorim’s moves tonight. He got the starting eleven spot on, waited with the substitutions, and gave his players good advice at the interval to avoid another push from Inter in the second half.

#2160. West Ham Insider Reveals Nuno’s Striker Gamble Before Sacking

Following the dismissal of Nuno Espírito Santo, questions are inevitably being asked about what went wrong during his time at West Ham United. And while there are plenty of areas worth examining, one of the most revealing concerns the Hammers’ striking department.

As Claret & Hugh learned from a West Ham insider before Nuno’s departure, the club’s three recognised centre-forwards were all specifically wanted by the Portuguese coach. That information is particularly significant given the team’s struggles in front of goal and the manager’s apparent reluctance to use some of the players he recruited.

The source’s assessment was straightforward: “They were all Nuno’s picks.”

It is a revelation that makes some of the decisions taken during the Championship campaign even harder to understand, particularly now that the manager has paid the price for West Ham’s disappointing performances.

The transfers attributed to recruitment director Nils Koppen have enjoyed varying degrees of success, and I still believe the jury is out on whether West Ham overpaid for Arne Engels.

But as Koppen himself explained, he had a very short period of time at the London Stadium before the summer transfer window closed.

What is not in doubt, according to our source, is that Nuno wanted Taty Castellanos, Pablo and Joël Piroe.

And it is the situation surrounding Piroe that I find particularly interesting.

“Nuno pushed really hard for Piroe because of his Championship goalscoring record. I’m surprised he hasn’t played more.”

Nuno pushed hard for Piroe but didn’t play him

Piroe arrived with a proven record of scoring goals in the Championship, something West Ham desperately needed following relegation.

Yet despite the Hammers’ continuing struggles in front of goal, he was given relatively limited opportunities to establish himself.

If Nuno was so determined to sign him, why was he so reluctant to play him?

It’s a perfectly reasonable question, particularly when neither Castellanos nor Pablo has done enough to make himself indispensable.

As we have already highlighted, the constant chopping and changing in attack did little to help any of West Ham’s forwards find form.

And if all three were Nuno’s preferred signings, it becomes considerably harder to blame the recruitment department for the lack of goals.

There had also been growing concern behind the scenes at the London Stadium that Espírito Santo did not know his best team.

It was a criticism supporters had been making for some time, and one that became increasingly difficult to dismiss as the manager continued changing personnel and formations.

The defeat against West Bromwich Albion provided another example of a team struggling for cohesion, creativity and confidence.

Ordinarily, in times gone by at West Ham, a certain amount of player frustration would eventually find its way back to David Sullivan.

Whether that happened in this instance remains unclear, particularly given the uncertainty surrounding the club’s ownership and decision-making structure.

But irrespective of any input from players, it had become increasingly evident that concerns were growing within the Hammers hierarchy.

The subsequent decision to dismiss Nuno confirms that the board believed a change was necessary, although it does not establish which individual concerns proved decisive.

Of course, Nuno’s departure doesn’t magically solve West Ham’s goalscoring problems.

Castellanos, Pablo and Piroe remain at the club, and whoever takes over will have to find a way of getting considerably more from them.

But that is also what makes the appointment of a new manager so interesting.

We have spent months wondering whether the problem was the players themselves or the way they were being used.

Now somebody else will have an opportunity to find out.

And perhaps the most revealing test will be what happens to Piroe, the proven Championship goalscorer whom Nuno apparently wanted so badly but seemed so reluctant to select.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#2159. Max Dowman suspension leaves Arsenal facing another selection headache after appeal rejection

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

The Football Association has rejected Arsenal’s appeal against Max Dowman’s red card at Fleetwood Town, meaning the 16-year-old will serve a three-match suspension.

Dowman was sent off during Tuesday’s Carabao Cup defeat, leaving Mikel Arteta with another attacking selection headache. Arsenal are already without several wide players through injury.

In the 85th minute of the match, Dowman received a red card for responding to a heavy challenge by Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal. Although he did not make a full kicking motion, his foot made contact with Neal.

The decision was a costly one for Arsenal, who were already struggling in the game against their League Two opponents. They lost the game 1-1 and then saw Fleetwood win the penalty shootout 5-3.

They lodged an appeal on Wednesday but have now been turned down, meaning Dowman will miss the next three games.

Dowman’s absence adds to Arsenal’s current problems in the wide areas.

That is three injured players with Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis all sidelined. It means there aren’t many attacking options for Arteta to choose from.

But they have a big game coming up on Sunday when they go to Liverpool. Arteta will need to decide who he is going to play.

Dowman had another chance to shine in the game against Fleetwood. However, he only started for the second time this season. It was somewhat of a controversial night for the teenager.

This is the second time Dowman has received a red card in a short space of time having been sent off while playing for England Under-19s earlier this month.

The latest dismissal has also shone a light on how Arsenal deal with one of their brightest young stars.

As Dowman made his way to the touchline, Arteta looked frustrated. He gave a serious look to the young teen and appeared to say something in anger as he exited the pitch.

This suggests it was something that had been discussed prior to the game. Arteta later said that the coaching staff had spoken about the emotional demands of the game during their preparations.

The Arsenal manager said the players had received clear instructions about what they needed to respect and control emotionally.

The dismissal was due to violent conduct. The laws of football state that a red card can be shown if a player uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality on an opponent, outside of a challenge for the ball.

This does not necessarily mean there has to be physical contact. In this case there was contact between Dowman and Neal.

The teen will miss the next three matches as a result of his ban. The focus will be on getting Arsenal ready for their Liverpool match with a lack of attacking options at their disposal.

For Dowman, it is important to avoid any further disciplinary issues.

He has made a few senior appearances already, thanks to his talent, but avoiding disqualification is also necessary for his growth as a player.

Arsenal have been dealt a potential setback in their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi. The Cherries are reportedly refusing to consider a January sale.

The Gunners are not alone in keeping an eye on the 20-year-old after he returned from injury. Manchester United have also made enquiries, and Tottenham remains a strong possibility after chasing him over the summer.

However, Bournemouth are keen to keep Kroupi at the Vitality Stadium following the January transfer window. His return will provide new head coach Marco Rose with another attacking threat. Helping to improve their position in the Premier League.

This could mean that Arsenal will have to plan a long-term pursuit of the player.

Kroupi provided a positive impression in his debut season in English football. Becoming one of the most exciting young forwards in the Premier League.

Overall, he hit the target on 13 occasions in the previous league campaign. Attracting the attention of a number of top European clubs.

Paris Saint Germain, Barcelona, Chelsea and Tottenham were among the clubs that were said to keep following his progress over the summer months.

However, he was unable to make the move after suffering an injury to his foot which required surgery. Kroupi has now returned to action. He came on as a late substitute in Bournemouth’s 3-0 victory against Manchester United last weekend.

Arsenal have again been linked. The Gunners are now known to be one of a number of clubs to have asked about the player’s injury and fitness ahead of improving their attacking options.

Tottenham are also interested, having had previous interest in signing him. There is no real suggestion an offer has been made.

They will also look to keep their attacking unit intact. Players such as Rayan and Marcus Tavernier are ones that Bournemouth will look to keep hold of. Alex Scott may also catch the eye of other clubs ahead of the New Year.

Bournemouth will be desperate to avoid losing a number of key players in one transfer window.

That stance leaves Arsenal facing a difficult decision if they want to pursue Kroupi. The Gunners can continue monitoring his performances and fitness, but a January move currently looks unlikely.

The forward’s return to regular football will give interested clubs another opportunity to assess his progress. Arsenal, Tottenham and Manchester United could therefore remain attentive to developments as the season continues.

Bournemouth are currently in the best position and Arsenal might have to wait until the summer to see how the Cherries will hold up when faced with losing one of their most promising young players.

#2156. “Welcome Back” Paco On The Market Following Dismissal | West Ham News

Former West Ham assistant coach Paco Jémez is once again searching for a new club after being relieved of his duties by Moroccan giants Raja Casablanca following a disappointing start to the season.

Jémez earned admirers for the attacking brand of football he implemented in Spain, and many supporters pointed to the turnaround in performances at West Ham as being credited to him.

However, his latest managerial venture has come to an abrupt end after Raja Casablanca opted to make a change just over two months after appointing him.

The club confirmed that Sunday’s 2-0 defeat to RS Berkane would be Jémez’s final match in charge, with officials deciding a fresh approach was needed after reviewing the team’s performances and results.

An official club statement explained that the sporting management felt a change in technical leadership was necessary to provide a new dynamic and improve the club’s chances of meeting its objectives this season.

Despite arriving in Casablanca with an impressive CV that included spells at Rayo Vallecano, Granada, Las Palmas and Mexican side Cruz Azul, the Spaniard struggled to generate momentum. Raja collected just six points from their opening five league fixtures, winning once, drawing three times and losing once.

Those results left his new club down in 13th place and under growing pressure, a situation made worse by a run of performances that failed to convince supporters.

Reports in Morocco had suggested Jémez’s future was already under scrutiny before the defeat against Berkane, with the coach reportedly asking club officials for more time to improve results. However, the latest setback proved decisive.

Following the defeat, Jémez accepted responsibility and apologised to supporters, acknowledging that the team had not produced the level of performance expected from one of Morocco’s biggest clubs. He also stated that he would accept whatever decision the board deemed appropriate.

West Ham ultimately went in a different direction by appointing Rui Pedro Silva as assistant head coach in the summer, despite Jémez publicly stating he wanted to stay on. Yet as of this morning, things have moved on!

Jémez’s latest dismissal serves as a reminder of the ruthless nature of football management.

#2155. Arsenal could expose Liverpool’s biggest weakness at Anfield

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have spent years struggling to impose themselves at Anfield. However, Mikel Arteta could have an opportunity to change that record when his side face Liverpool on Sunday.

The Gunners have often struggled against the physicality of Liverpool on Merseyside. Since Jurgen Klopp took charge, Liverpool have built a reputation for being high pressing, fast, and making their opponents make mistakes.

However, looking at the latest stats, it seems that Liverpool are no longer as physical, meaning that Arsenal could target their weaknesses.

The disparity is stark between the two teams, with Liverpool having run the least distance of any Premier League side this season. Meanwhile, Arsenal are running the most.

If Arteta’s side can capitalise on this and create fast attacks from possession, then they can utilise this to their advantage.

Liverpool have shifted away from their high-octane style associated with much of Klopp’s reign. Arne Slot has slowly moved towards a more possession-based approach, focusing on keeping the ball.

Andoni Iraola looks keen to add more intensity to their pressing. The Reds have had some of the best pressing stats in the Premier League this season (Opta Analyst).

However, they are not getting the desired intensity from the system.

In addition to chasing the opposition when they have the ball, players must quickly recover, cut off passing lanes and return to their defensive positions.

This is where Arsenal might have an opportunity. If they can get past Liverpool’s first line of pressure, they may have space to push forward before the home side can get back into position.

Another area that the Gunners could target is Liverpool’s midfield.

Alexis MacAllister and Ryan Gravenberch are technically gifted and very composed when they have the ball. But neither are a true defensive midfielder, which raises questions over their ability to stop teams playing through the middle.

Arsenal have the players to exploit this. Declan Rice can put in an energetic, physical performance and drive the play forward. Myles Lewis-Skelly provides another option who can run with the ball into dangerous areas.

This can cause problems for the Liverpool midfield. Arsenal can try to disrupt Mac Allister and Gravenberch, not letting them set the tempo of the game.

If they win these individual battles, it can stop Liverpool from getting the ball control they want.

The task is certainly a tall one. Arsenal have lost their last 16 games at Anfield, including seven in Arteta’s reign.

Whilst that may be the case, the current Liverpool team are very different to the one Arsenal have faced on a regular basis during Klopp’s time in charge.

They certainly can’t expect to be outplayed, but they must take advantage of Liverpool’s failings.

Arsenal are currently second in the Premier League with 21 points from eight games. They will want to win here but will need to do more than just run them into the ground.

If Rice and Lewis-Skelly can push forward and pressurise them, forcing them to make mistakes, then Arteta could finally have his winning recipe at Anfield.

#2154. Arsenal news: Arsenal vs Liverpool. Arteta targets Anfield record as Liverpool prepare for Premier League clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal vs Liverpool: Arsenal travel to Anfield on Sunday looking to maintain their strong start to the Premier League season and end a long wait for victory at Liverpool’s home ground.

A blistering start to the season has seen Mikel Arteta’s side win seven of their first eight league games, leaving them tied on points with Manchester City at the top of the table and six points ahead of Liverpool going into the game.

However, the Gunners have not beaten Liverpool in the Premier League at Anfield since 2012/13. Arteta will be aware that the Reds are starting to gel under Andoni Iraola.

They have won three of their last four league games after a lacklustre start and had their first league win at home this season with their 2-0 win over Brighton.

After replacing Arne Slot over the summer, Iraola brought his impressive three-year spell at Bournemouth to Anfield. However, Liverpool have struggled to adjust to the new manager, losing 3 of their first 4 league games.

But they have recently improved and are looking to play a much faster style of football. As Adrian Clarke notes, they are pressing more, not sitting back as much and wanting to attack quickly when they win the ball.

They have been the most direct attackers in the Premier League. They have pace to spare within their attack, with players like Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo providing a threat in advanced areas.

Isak comes into the game in good form after finding the back of the net six times in his first eight league games. He has scored in three successive games in the Premier League for the first time since joining the club.

Florian Wirtz will also play a key role in Liverpool’s attacking play. The German has been consistently creating chances for the team playing behind Isak in a 4-2-3-1 system. He has created nine chances against Brentford.

Arsenal will need to limit the space available to Liverpool’s forward players. Allowing Isak and Gakpo to combine freely could make an already difficult away fixture even harder.

Arsenal have had some positive news on their squad ahead of their Merseyside trip. Declan Rice and Riccardo Calafiori are both back in training.

Christos Tzolis has also trained after missing October. Noni Madueke has also not been ruled out by Arteta ahead of Sunday’s match after he missed the Fleetwood game.

They also have their own fitness issues to contend with. Iraola confirmed that Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz are both available after suffering injuries earlier in the month.

Jeramie Frimpong will be missing due to a hamstring issue but should be back after the international break. Hugo Ekitike, Geovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley are all still sidelined with longer-term injuries.

The presence of Rice will be key for Arsenal. He has been one of the best progressive midfielders in the Premier League, along with their captain, Martin Odegaard.

Despite losing just one of their last eight Premier League clashes against Liverpool, Arsenal are not as strong on the road.

The Gunners have not won any league games in their last 13 trips to Anfield. They have drawn five and lost eight. Their last win was a 2-0 victory back in the 2012/13 season.

They have also never gone 14 games unbeaten away from home in the league. That would be a great achievement.

However, there is good reason to believe they can do it. They have only conceded five clean sheets in the league this season. They have faced the least number of shots on target and the fewest expected goals.

Liverpool have also been on a strong run defensively with four clean sheets in their last six league games, so Arsenal must make their chances count.

A win would provide another key result against a direct rival, improving their position at the top of the Premier League table and finally putting an end to one of the clubs’ longest-running away day woes.
